activities.description: Walk through the Tegallalang Rice Terraces and grab a smoothie bowl at Alchemy café in central Ubud
Explore the Sacred Monkey Forest Sanctuary then browse artisan shops along Jalan Hanoman
Watch a traditional Kecak fire dance at Ubud Royal Palace and dine at Locavore for modern Indonesian cuisine
Visit Tirta Empul water temple for a Balinese purification ritual
Chase waterfalls at Tegenungan and cool off with a swim at the base pool
Sunset dinner at Swept Away restaurant overlooking the Ayung River valley
Drive to Seminyak and start with brunch at Sisterfields on Jalan Kayu Aya
Relax at Potato Head Beach Club with ocean views, infinity pool, and cocktails
Catch the legendary sunset from La Plancha beach bar then dinner at Mama San
Sunrise trek up Mount Batur volcano — your guide meets you at 3:30am for the 2-hour hike to the summit
Soak in the Toya Devasya natural hot springs at the base of Mount Batur
Explore Sidemen village for a quiet dinner at Warung Wayan with valley views
Head south and grab breakfast at The Loft in Canggu on the way down
Surf or sunbathe at Padang Padang Beach, the hidden cove from Eat Pray Love
Sunset Kecak dance at Uluwatu Temple perched on 70-meter cliffs, then grilled seafood on Jimbaran Bay beach
Visit the Grand Palace and Wat Phra Kaew (Temple of the Emerald Buddha) — arrive early at 8:30am to beat crowds
Cross the Chao Phraya River by ferry to Wat Arun and climb the central prang for panoramic views
Street food crawl through Chinatown's Yaowarat Road — try the famous oyster omelets and mango sticky rice
Take a longtail boat tour through Thonburi canals to see traditional stilt houses and floating vendors
Explore the massive Chatuchak Weekend Market — over 15,000 stalls across 35 sections
Rooftop drinks at Sky Bar at Lebua State Tower, then dinner at Err Urban Rustic Thai near Wat Pho
Visit Wat Pho to see the 46-meter reclining Buddha, then get a traditional Thai massage on-site
Explore the trendy Ari neighborhood — lunch at Pla Dib for fresh sashimi and browse indie boutiques
Night market dinner at Jodd Fairs near Rama 9, famous for crab pad thai and grilled seafood
Early drive to Damnoen Saduak Floating Market — paddle through canals and eat pad thai from a boat
Stop at the Maeklong Railway Market where vendors fold up stalls as trains pass inches away
Back in Bangkok for dinner at Thipsamai on Mahachai Road — the city's most famous pad thai
Visit the Jim Thompson House museum — a stunning teak home filled with Southeast Asian art
World-class Thai massage at Wat Pho Traditional Medical School, then explore the hip Talat Noi street art district
Farewell dinner at Jay Fai, the legendary street food stall with a Michelin star — try the drunken noodles and crab omelet
Start at Meiji Shrine in Yoyogi Park for a peaceful walk through towering torii gates and old-growth forest
Explore Harajuku's Takeshita Street for kawaii culture, then walk Omotesando for upscale architecture and boutiques
Cross the iconic Shibuya Scramble, then head to Shibuya Yokocho food alley for yakitori and highballs
Breakfast at Tsukiji Outer Market — fresh sushi at Sushi Dai or tamagoyaki from Yamachou
Walk through upscale Ginza district and visit teamLab Borderless digital art museum in Azabudai Hills
Explore the neon-lit streets of Akihabara for anime culture, then ramen at Fuunji in Shinjuku
Visit Senso-ji temple in Asakusa — walk through the Kaminarimon thunder gate and browse Nakamise shopping street
Cross the Sumida River to Tokyo Skytree for 360-degree views, then explore the quirky shops of Shimokitazawa
Bar-hop through the tiny Golden Gai alleyways in Shinjuku — each bar seats only 6-8 people
Stroll through Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden — one of Tokyo's most beautiful parks with Japanese and French gardens
Take the train to Yanaka, Tokyo's old-town neighborhood with traditional shotengai shopping streets and cat statues
Dinner under the Shinjuku train tracks at Omoide Yokocho (Memory Lane) — smoky yakitori joints since the 1940s
Early morning tuna auction viewing at Toyosu Fish Market, then sushi breakfast at one of the market restaurants
Cross Rainbow Bridge to Odaiba for the life-size Unicorn Gundam statue and Miraikan science museum
Final dinner in Ebisu at Afuri for their signature yuzu shio ramen, then drinks at a hidden speakeasy in Roppongi
Arrive early at Fushimi Inari Shrine to walk through thousands of vermillion torii gates up the mountain trail
Visit Kiyomizu-dera temple for stunning hilltop views, then stroll down the preserved streets of Ninenzaka and Sannenzaka
Dinner in the Gion district — try kaiseki dining at Gion Karyo, then walk Hanami-koji for possible geisha sightings
Visit Kinkaku-ji (Golden Pavilion) reflected in its mirror pond — one of Japan's most iconic sights
Meditate at Ryoan-ji's famous rock garden, then walk to Ninna-ji temple through quiet residential streets
Explore Nishiki Market (Kyoto's kitchen) for street food — try yuba, matcha treats, and pickled vegetables
Walk through the ethereal Arashiyama Bamboo Grove at sunrise before the crowds arrive
Cross the Togetsukyo Bridge, visit the monkey park on Mount Iwatayama, and explore Tenryu-ji temple gardens
Traditional tofu kaiseki dinner at Shoraian, a riverside restaurant in Arashiyama accessible only by boat
Walk the Philosopher's Path along the canal lined with cherry and maple trees to Ginkaku-ji (Silver Pavilion)
Attend a traditional tea ceremony in the Uji district — Japan's most famous matcha-growing region
Cross the river to Pontocho Alley for dinner at a tiny riverside restaurant with yuka terrace dining over the Kamogawa
Explore the moss-covered grounds of Gio-ji temple, then nearby Adashino Nenbutsu-ji with its 8,000 stone statues
Visit Tofuku-ji temple for its stunning bridge views, then browse vintage kimono shops in the Teramachi arcade
Farewell dinner at Kyoto's Ramen Koji food floor in Kyoto Station — try the rich tonkotsu at Masutani
Climb the Eiffel Tower early (book the 9am slot online), then stroll through Champ de Mars gardens
Walk across Pont Alexandre III to the Champs-Elysees, then up to the Arc de Triomphe rooftop for city views
Dinner in Saint-Germain-des-Pres at Le Comptoir du Pantheon, then evening walk along the illuminated Seine
Spend the morning at the Louvre — head straight to the Winged Victory, then Mona Lisa, then the Egyptian wing
Explore Le Marais neighborhood — falafel at L'As du Fallafel on Rue des Rosiers, then browse vintage shops
Cocktails at Candelaria (hidden bar behind a taqueria), then dinner at Breizh Cafe for savory buckwheat crepes
Climb to Sacre-Coeur basilica in Montmartre, then wander the cobblestone streets around Place du Tertre
Visit Musee d'Orsay for the world's best Impressionist collection — Monet, Renoir, Van Gogh all in one building
Wine and cheese at a cave a manger in the 11th arrondissement, try Le Verre Vole near Canal Saint-Martin
Take the RER C train to Versailles — explore the Hall of Mirrors and State Apartments before noon crowds
Wander the gardens of Versailles, rent a rowboat on the Grand Canal, and visit Marie Antoinette's Hamlet
Back in Paris for dinner at Bouillon Chartier — a stunning Belle Epoque dining hall with classic French dishes at local prices
Browse the Shakespeare and Company bookshop, then coffee and croissants at Cafe de Flore in Saint-Germain
Explore the Latin Quarter — visit the Pantheon, Luxembourg Gardens, and pick up macarons at Pierre Herme
Sunset cruise on the Seine with Bateaux Mouches, then farewell dinner at Le Bouillon Pigalle in the 18th
Tour the Colosseum with underground access (book ahead), then walk through the Roman Forum ruins
Climb Palatine Hill for views over the Forum, then toss a coin in the Trevi Fountain
Dinner in Trastevere — try the cacio e pepe at Da Enzo al 29 (arrive early, there's always a line)
Early entry to the Vatican Museums — rush through to the Sistine Chapel first, then double back to explore the galleries
Climb to the top of St. Peter's Basilica dome for breathtaking views, then explore Castel Sant'Angelo
Aperitivo hour in the Prati neighborhood near the Vatican, then dinner at Pizzarium for Rome's best pizza al taglio
Visit the Pantheon at opening time when light streams through the oculus, then espresso at Sant'Eustachio Il Caffe
Wander from Piazza Navona to Campo de' Fiori market, grab suppli (fried rice balls) at Supplizio
Sunset walk to the Spanish Steps, then dinner in the Jewish Ghetto — try the fried artichokes at Nonna Betta
Timed entry at Galleria Borghese to see Bernini's sculptures and Caravaggio paintings in a stunning villa
Stroll through Villa Borghese gardens, rent a rowboat on the lake, then walk down to Piazza del Popolo
Explore the foodie neighborhood of Testaccio — street food at Mercato Testaccio, then pasta at Felice a Testaccio
Rent a bike and ride the ancient Appian Way past ruins, catacombs, and Roman aqueducts
Visit the Capuchin Crypt beneath Santa Maria della Concezione, then gelato at Fatamorgana near Piazza di Spagna
Farewell dinner at Roscioli — their carbonara is legendary, and the wine cellar has over 2,600 labels
Visit La Sagrada Familia — book the tower access for jaw-dropping views of the spiraling staircases and city
Explore Park Guell's mosaic terraces and Gaudi's gingerbread-style gatehouses with panoramic city views
Tapas crawl through Gracia neighborhood — try Bar Bodega Quimet for vermouth and patatas bravas
Get lost in the Gothic Quarter's medieval lanes — visit the Barcelona Cathedral and Placa Reial
Browse La Boqueria market on Las Ramblas for fresh juices, jamon iberico, and seafood cones
Dinner at Cal Pep near the waterfront for some of the best tapas in the city — sit at the bar for the full experience
Walk along Barceloneta Beach, then brunch at La Mar Salada with views of the marina
Explore the El Born neighborhood — visit the Picasso Museum, then browse indie boutiques on Carrer del Rec
Sunset drinks at a rooftop bar in the Born, then dinner at El Xampanyet for cava and anchovies
Take the cable car up Montjuic hill to the castle for sweeping views of the harbor and city
Visit the Fundacio Joan Miro, then walk down through the gardens to the Magic Fountain
Stroll the Eixample district to see Casa Batllo and Casa Mila lit up at night, then pintxos at Cerveceria Catalana
Visit the Sant Pau Art Nouveau complex — a stunning former hospital that rivals Gaudi's work
Explore the Poblenou neighborhood's street art and converted warehouses, lunch at Els Quatre Gats
Farewell paella at La Mar Salada on the beach, then walk the Olympic Port as the sun sets
Ride Tram 28 through the winding streets, then walk up to Sao Jorge Castle for panoramic views
Get lost in Alfama's labyrinth of alleys — visit the Lisbon Cathedral (Se) and stop for ginjinha at A Ginjinha
Dinner at a traditional tasca in Alfama, then live Fado music at Clube de Fado or Mesa de Frades
Take the tram to Belem — visit Jeronimos Monastery, then eat the original pasteis de nata at Pasteis de Belem
Explore the Tower of Belem and the Monument to the Discoveries along the Tagus River waterfront
Head to LX Factory, a converted industrial complex with restaurants, bookshops, and rooftop bars
Ride the Santa Justa Elevator for city views, then coffee at A Brasileira in Chiado where Pessoa used to sit
Browse the Feira da Ladra flea market, then explore the street art and miradouros of Graca
Dinner at Cervejaria Ramiro for the best seafood in Lisbon — the garlic shrimp and steak sandwich chaser are legendary
Train to Sintra (40 min) — visit the colorful Pena Palace perched on a hilltop surrounded by forest
Explore the mystical Quinta da Regaleira with its initiatic well, underground tunnels, and gardens
Back in Lisbon for dinner in the Santos neighborhood — try O Velho Eurico for hearty Portuguese comfort food
Walk along the riverfront from Cais do Sodre to the Time Out Market for a brunch of Portuguese specialties
Cross the Tagus by ferry to Cacilhas for views of the 25 de Abril Bridge, then visit the Cristo Rei statue
Farewell sunset drinks at Miradouro da Graca, then dinner at Taberna da Rua das Flores for petiscos
Dive into the Medina souks — start at Souk Semmarine and wind through the leather, spice, and textile sections
Visit the Bahia Palace with its intricate zellij tilework and painted cedar ceilings
Watch the sunset circus at Jemaa el-Fnaa square — snake charmers, storytellers, and dozens of food stalls firing up
Wander the Jardin Majorelle — Yves Saint Laurent's cobalt blue garden with cacti and a Berber museum
Visit the Saadian Tombs and the ruins of El Badi Palace, once covered in gold and onyx
Rooftop dinner at Nomad in the Medina with views over the spice market — try the lamb tangia and harira soup
Drive 90 minutes to the Atlas Mountains — hike through Berber villages in the Ourika Valley
Lunch at a family-run Berber home with tagine and mint tea, then visit the Setti Fatma waterfalls
Back in Marrakech for a traditional hammam experience at Les Bains de Marrakech spa
Take a Moroccan cooking class in a riad — learn to make tagine, couscous, and preserved lemons from scratch
Visit the Museum of Marrakech in the old Ben Youssef Medersa, then explore the tanneries in the northern Medina
Dinner at Al Fassia — a famous restaurant run entirely by women, known for the best traditional Moroccan cuisine in the city
Explore the Mellah (Jewish Quarter) and visit the Lazama Synagogue, then browse the spice market at Rahba Kedima
Visit Le Jardin Secret, a beautifully restored riad garden in the heart of the Medina with a rooftop tower view
Farewell dinner at Dar Yacout — a palatial riad restaurant with live Gnawa music and a multi-course Moroccan feast
Take the rotating cable car up Table Mountain — hike the short summit trail for 360-degree views of the Cape
Explore the V&A Waterfront — visit the Zeitz MOCAA contemporary African art museum in a converted grain silo
Sunset drinks at the Silo Hotel rooftop bar, then dinner at The Pot Luck Club in the Woodstock neighborhood
Drive Chapman's Peak — one of the world's most scenic coastal roads — to Cape Point and the lighthouse
Visit the penguin colony at Boulders Beach in Simon's Town, then fish and chips at Kalky's
Dinner in Kalk Bay at Harbour House with ocean views, then browse the quirky antique shops along Main Road
Drive to Stellenbosch — South Africa's most beautiful wine town surrounded by mountains and vineyards
Wine tasting at Delaire Graff estate with mountain views, then Babylonstoren for their famous garden lunch
Dinner in Franschhoek at La Petite Colombe, one of South Africa's top restaurants, then drive back to Cape Town
Walk the colorful streets of Bo-Kaap — take a Cape Malay cooking class and learn to make bobotie and samoosas
Visit Robben Island by ferry — tour Nelson Mandela's former cell led by a former political prisoner
Dinner at The Test Kitchen in Woodstock or La Colombe for creative South African fine dining
Hike Lion's Head at sunrise for incredible views of Table Mountain, the city, and both oceans
Relax at Camps Bay beach backed by the Twelve Apostles mountain range, lunch at Codfather for fresh seafood
Farewell sundowners at Beta Beach in Bakoven, then braai dinner at Mzansi in Woodstock
Seaplane transfer from Male airport to your atoll — the aerial views of turquoise rings in the Indian Ocean are unforgettable
Settle into your overwater bungalow, snorkel directly from your deck over the house reef
Welcome dinner on the beach with feet in the sand, fresh grilled lobster and reef fish under the stars
Guided snorkel safari to spot sea turtles, reef sharks, and manta rays at a nearby reef channel
Try a beginner scuba dive or semi-submarine tour to see coral gardens without getting wet
Floating dinner on a platform in the lagoon, or sunset cocktails at the overwater bar
Speedboat to a local Maldivian island to visit the village, market, and see how locals live outside the resorts
Stop at a pristine sandbank in the middle of the ocean for swimming and a picnic lunch
Sunset dolphin cruise — spinner dolphins are common and often leap alongside the boat
Overwater spa treatment — traditional Maldivian massage with coconut oil while waves lap beneath you
Kayak or stand-up paddleboard across the lagoon, then hammock time with a book on the beach
Night snorkeling to see bioluminescent plankton glowing in the shallow water along the beach
Sunrise yoga on the beach, then a final snorkel session over the house reef to say goodbye to the fish
Explore Male if time allows — visit the fish market, Hukuru Miskiy mosque, and the colorful waterfront buildings
Farewell dinner at a Male local restaurant like Sala Thai or Symphony for a mix of Maldivian and Asian cuisine
Walk to Hallgrimskirkja church for views from the tower, then stroll the colorful Laugavegur shopping street
Visit Harpa Concert Hall's stunning glass architecture, then the National Museum of Iceland for Viking history
Dinner at Grillid for modern Icelandic cuisine, then bar-hop along Laugavegur — Reykjavik's nightlife starts late
Drive to Thingvellir National Park — walk between the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates
Watch Strokkur geyser erupt every 5-8 minutes at Geysir, then visit the powerful Gullfoss waterfall
Soak in the Secret Lagoon in Fludir — a smaller, more authentic alternative to the Blue Lagoon
Drive to Seljalandsfoss waterfall — you can walk behind the curtain of water — then nearby Skogafoss
Walk on Reynisfjara black sand beach with its dramatic basalt columns and roaring Atlantic waves
Dinner in the village of Vik, then drive back watching for Northern Lights if visiting in winter
Join a glacier hike on Solheimajokull — strap on crampons and walk across ancient blue ice with a guide
Drive to Jokulsarlon glacier lagoon to see icebergs calving into the lake, then Diamond Beach where ice washes ashore
Dinner in Hofn, the lobster capital of Iceland — try langoustine soup at Pakkhus restaurant
Visit the Sky Lagoon near Reykjavik for their 7-step spa ritual with cold plunge and ocean views
Last walk around Reykjavik — visit the Sun Voyager sculpture, Grandi food hall for a lamb hot dog at Baejarins Beztu
Farewell dinner at Dill, Iceland's Michelin-starred restaurant featuring New Nordic cuisine with Icelandic ingredients
Arrive in Cusco at 3,400m altitude — take it slow with coca tea and a gentle walk around Plaza de Armas
Visit the Qorikancha (Temple of the Sun) where Inca gold walls once reflected sunlight across the city
Dinner at Cicciolina on Calle Triunfo — try alpaca steak and a pisco sour in a cozy colonial setting
Drive to the Sacred Valley — visit the Pisac ruins and the vibrant Pisac artisan market
Explore the Moray circular Inca terraces (an ancient agricultural lab), then the Maras salt mines with thousands of pink terraced pools
Stay overnight in Ollantaytambo — wander the living Inca town and dine at Hearts Cafe
Take the early PeruRail Vistadome train to Aguas Calientes, then bus up the switchbacks to Machu Picchu at sunrise
Guided tour of the citadel — Sun Temple, Intihuatana stone, Temple of Three Windows — then hike Huayna Picchu if you booked a permit
Train back to Ollantaytambo or Cusco — dinner at El Indio Feliz in Aguas Calientes if you stay overnight
Walk up to the massive Sacsayhuaman fortress above Cusco — the zig-zag stone walls weigh up to 200 tons each
Explore the San Pedro Market for fresh juices, cheese empanadas, and choclo con queso (giant corn with cheese)
Peruvian cooking class in San Blas neighborhood, then drinks at Museo del Pisco for creative pisco cocktails
Early drive to Vinicunca (Rainbow Mountain) — the 2-hour hike to 5,200m rewards you with striped, multicolored peaks
Return to Cusco and recover with a traditional Andean massage, then browse artisan textile shops in San Blas
Farewell dinner at MAP Cafe inside the Museo de Arte Precolombino — fine dining surrounded by ancient art
Walk across the Brooklyn Bridge at sunrise, then grab coffee and a croissant at Time Out Market in DUMBO
Explore Lower Manhattan — 9/11 Memorial pools, Wall Street, then ferry to the Statue of Liberty and Ellis Island
Dinner in the West Village at Via Carota for Italian, then walk the High Line park lit up at night
Visit the Met Museum on the Upper East Side — the Egyptian Temple of Dendur and Impressionist wing are must-sees
Walk through Central Park — Bethesda Fountain, Bow Bridge, Strawberry Fields, then over to Columbus Circle
See a Broadway show in the Theater District, then late-night pizza at Joe's Pizza on Carmine Street
Explore Williamsburg — walk Bedford Avenue for vintage shops, then brunch at Sunday in Brooklyn for their famous pancakes
Street art tour in Bushwick, then take the L train to Smorgasburg food market on the waterfront
Cocktails at Westlight rooftop bar in Williamsburg for skyline views, then dinner at Lilia for handmade pasta
Shop and stroll through SoHo's cast-iron architecture on Greene and Broome streets, coffee at La Colombe
Visit the Whitney Museum of American Art in the Meatpacking District, then browse Chelsea Market for food and gifts
Dinner at Los Tacos No. 1 in Chelsea Market, then live jazz at the Village Vanguard in Greenwich Village
Visit the Guggenheim Museum's spiral rotunda on the Upper East Side, then bagels at Russ and Daughters on the Lower East Side
Explore Harlem — gospel brunch at Sylvia's Restaurant, then walk past the Apollo Theater and brownstone-lined streets
Farewell dinner at Le Bernardin for world-class seafood, then Top of the Rock at sunset for your last NYC panorama
Explore the blue-domed churches of Oia — walk the marble lanes and find the iconic three-dome viewpoint
Descend the 300 steps to Ammoudi Bay for lunch at Sunset Ammoudi taverna — grilled octopus right off the boat
Claim your spot for the famous Oia sunset at the castle ruins, then dinner at Lauda for caldera-view fine dining
Walk the caldera path from Fira to Imerovigli — 3km of stunning cliff-edge views of the volcanic crater
Take a boat tour to the volcanic islands — hike Nea Kameni's crater and swim in the hot springs of Palea Kameni
Dinner at Koukoumavlos in Fira for creative Greek cuisine, then drinks at Tango Bar on the caldera edge
Visit Red Beach near Akrotiri — dramatic red volcanic cliffs meeting crystal-clear water
Wine tasting at Santo Wines or Venetsanos Winery — try the crisp Assyrtiko grape unique to Santorini's volcanic soil
Dinner in the hilltop village of Pyrgos at Selene restaurant, one of the island's most celebrated tables
Visit Akrotiri archaeological site — a Minoan city buried by volcanic eruption in 1600 BC, the Greek Pompeii
Relax at Perissa Black Sand Beach — lounge at a beach bar and swim in the warm Aegean
Meze dinner at To Psaraki in Vlychada port — fresh seafood in a no-frills harbor setting the locals love
Take a small boat to Thirassia island — Santorini's quiet, untouristy neighbor with whitewashed villages and no crowds
Back in Santorini, explore Megalochori village with its traditional cave houses and cava wine cellars
Farewell dinner at Ambrosia in Oia — reserve a balcony table for one last legendary Santorini sunset
